statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so there is no current price path to score. Friday's inside-range close, a rotational two-way session and a VIX near the low end of its 52-week range keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. One window is flagged: the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where a weekend in which Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day Hormuz reopening plan and Iranian anti-ship missile fire at the strait was reported meets a 10-year yield at 5.18% and the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; rejected Hormuz plan and fresh missile reports frame the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's session: front NQ futures settled at 30,889.25, up 0.40%, inside a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, while the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 13.38-35.30 52-week range. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%), which snapped a three-week losing streak and delivered the first winning week in three.

Friday's internals remain the clearest evidence against a pathological path. Delayed latest-session context shows Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%, with Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +1.76%, Semiconductors +0.56% and Software - Infrastructure +1.19% against Software - Application -0.50%. Megacap dispersion was wide in the same delayed set, with Microsoft +3.66% against Meta -3.33%. A rotational session in which leadership changed hands while the index still closed higher is mean reversion working, not failing. That context is labelled non-real-time, its source as-of is not provided, and it cannot establish current NQ structure.

The macro backdrop is where Stress lives. The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 5.18%, described in Friday reporting as the highest since the financial crisis, with the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47% in the latest H.15 release for 24 September. Equities absorbed that bond move because oil eased: WTI fell 2.33% to $92.41 and is about 7.4% lower on the week, with Brent at $104.32, still roughly 20% higher on the month and 51% higher on the year. Federal funding is not a near-term catalyst, since the continuing resolution signed on 2 September runs to 11 December.

Two weekend developments arrived while the market was shut and therefore remain unpriced. On 26 September Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a plan that had been paired with an Iranian offer to readmit UN nuclear inspectors. Early on 27 September Iranian anti-ship missile fire at the strait was reported. Both sit inside a seven-month campaign that equity markets have repeatedly discounted, and neither is a discontinuity relative to Friday's pricing, so they raise Stress and cap Confidence rather than Tail. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where that unpriced news set meets the thinnest liquidity of the week. Tail would only leave the low band on observed evidence after the reopen: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or price holding near a session extreme.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 04:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 03:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 44 to 55 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 82 down to 71 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the nineteenth slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, drifts back toward 11 as the reopen approaches, and peaks at 18 in the reopen hour before easing to 15, 13, 11, 10 and 9 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 54 and 61 on a 10-year at its highest since the financial crisis, a rejected seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, reported weekend anti-ship missile fire at the strait, and crude about 7.4% lower on the week. Confidence decays to 62 in the last closed hours before recovering to 76 once roughly four hours of live tape exist. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is 22:00Z to 23:59Z.
